title: cn-candidate/v1 — a proposal for the conceptual model
description: One candidate in the cn promotion queue (cn contracts §6, AM-20): exactly one proposal (a concept, a term or an open-tier relation), where it came from, and what became of it. Source-agnostic: every producer (a document pipeline, a recipe synthesizer, an evidence miner, a steward) submits this one shape. A promoted candidate is a model TEXT change — `resolution.canon_ref` names the merged commit and the def it added or changed. The JVM enforcement is `org.tatrman.concept.candidate.CnCandidates` (ttr-concept); `CandidateSchemaSpec` holds the two to each other fixture by fixture.

status.description: `proposed` until a steward acts; `rejected` and `promoted` are final and carry a `resolution`.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 with an explicit offset. A calendar-impossible date (`2026-02-30`) passes this pattern and is refused by the JVM validator only.

name.description: A TTR identifier: a name the promotion writes as model text. A word the grammar reserves (`date`, `type`, `target`, …) matches this pattern and is refused by the JVM reader only — by the grammar's own `id` rule (`TtrId.isId`), so the list never drifts from `TTR.g4`.

locale.description: A label key or a lexicon file's locale (`model lexicon locale cs`).

line.description: One line of model text: a label or a surface form.

participant.description: One labelled participant of an event (`Encounter as from` is `{ concept: cn.Encounter, label: from }`).

sourceRef.description: Where a candidate or an evidence example came from (cn contracts §6, A-CN-82): `doc://<system>/<document>[#<locator>]` (a locator is `s<n>` — a sentence, 1-based; `r<n>` — a table row, 1-based; `c<start>-<end>` — a code-point span, 0-based, end exclusive), `recipe://<package>/<recipe>#s<n>` (a recipe sentence), `question://<system>/<question>`. A span whose end does not exceed its start passes this pattern and is refused by the JVM validator only.

concept.description: A new concept def. Which fields a stereotype takes follows the grammar (cn contracts §1.1): a role names its defining `event`; a phase and a quality name their bearer (`of`) and are defined OR grounded, never both. `definition_text` is a TTR-P definition expression — the body of `definition: """…"""`. `er_rendering` is filled at promotion, for a phase.

definition_text.description: Not blank, no triple quote. Blank means every character is whitespace, and whitespace is one explicit set — tab, LF, VT, FF, CR, space, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000–U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000, U+FEFF — never `\s`, whose meaning differs between the JDK, ECMA-262 and Python validators.

suggested_grounding.description: An md or er element the concept would ground to (`grounds:`); for a phase, a query-backed entity only.

term.description: Words for a concept (`def term … { for: cn.X, forms: […] }` in the lexicon file of `locale`). The target is a concept in the model (`target_qname`) or one still in the queue (`proposed_concept_ref` — that candidate's `id`; promotable once it is).

relation.description: An open-tier relation (cn contracts §1.3): `relations: [ { type: <type_name>, to: <to> } ]` on `from`. It never lowers.

producer.description: The producer id (`kleio`, `au:synthesizer`, `manual:<steward>`, `<deployment>:evidence`, `<deployment>:span-catalogue`). This schema checks the id's shape; which producers a store admits — and that an importer never does (L15-5) — is its registry's (`ProducerRegistry`, A-CN-83).

confidence.description: The resolver's Confidence shape: the number, who computed it, how.

evidence.description: AM-20 — why a steward should care. `text` is verbatim; de-identifying it is the producer's duty before it submits.

example.description: One piece of evidence. Its `ref` scheme follows its kind: a question is `question://`, a recipe sentence `recipe://`, a document and a processor's output (the span it read) `doc://`.

canon_ref.description: `<merged commit>:<qname>` — the def the promotion added (`cn.X`, `lexicon.<term>`) or changed (a relation's `from`).
